objective: Prove for laws on bits: pairwise laws have no knots and every circuit is a tie; two knots sharing one distinction compose into one knot on all their other distinctions exactly when they force it to opposite values, and are a hub otherwise; a knot forces values in one direction only exactly when it is 'not all on' or 'not all off'; in a law whose knots force both values, chains compose into knots growing with the chain; hence every law on bits is pairwise, frozen or transmitting, and laws of negative clauses, implications and unit literals (or the dual) are frozen. Check exhaustively on all knots of three and four variables and on every law generated by one relation on at most three bits.
status: Proved by BASE-THREE-20261021-001A-P001 (V1 prose proof with exhaustive checks; majority closure, resolution and Post's lattice cited). For laws on bits: pairwise laws have only ties; at every excluded pattern a knot forces each variable; two knots sharing one distinction compose into one knot on all their other distinctions exactly when they force it oppositely, and are a hub otherwise (10,404 of 10,404 placements); a knot forces one direction only exactly when it is 'not all on' or 'not all off' (2 of 34 and 2 of 742); so every law is pairwise, frozen or transmitting, and in transmitting laws chains grow by one per three-variable knot. Laws of negative clauses, implications and units are frozen; the converses are read from Post's lattice and checked on all 273 one-relation laws on at most three bits (183 pairwise, 2 frozen, 88 transmitting).
title: Proof: transmission and the three regimes
